preamble: squalify: a deterministic data-file profiler. It reads one file and writes a versioned JSON descriptor (structure, fields, statistics, layout, fingerprint, evidence) that other tools, such as DataBall, use to classify the file or pick a transform. Design: docs/design.md. Schema: docs/descriptor.md.

items.title: Consumer classification contract

note_records.text: **2026-10-26** — Packaging: the consumer prefers to reference squalify as a pinned NuGet package (decided on the consumer side, still open). If chosen, squalify needs a packaging item (package id, versioning, feed).

**2026-10-26** — **2026-10-26** — prism tie-in: the consumer subset should include per-field `nullTokens` with counts per token (prism D74/D77) and say how `NaN` is reported, since prism reads it as a number in `(unit)` columns (D38) while squalify vocabulary 1 treats it as null.

**2026-10-27** — **2026-10-27** — From sq-16 review: `-NaN`, `+NaN`, `Infinity` and `-Infinity` classify as `string` (only `NaN` is in the null vocabulary), so a prism `(unit)` column with them types as `string`; integers over ~309 digits are `string`, 20-309 digits `float`. Document or decide in the consumer contract.

**2026-10-27** — From sq-04: (1) format.dialect.quote is always " for delimited files (owner decision 10), so it is stable across ATE export files. (2) fields[] members not computed until sq-05/sq-14 are null (nameParts, nullTokens, flags, distinct, shapes, constant, unique); consumers must wait for those slices. (3) Known edge (architect probe G): a header-less comma CSV with a multi-word first column and an integer last column (Site North,3) can be taken as whitespace-delimited; with a header, comma wins. ATE export files always have a header.

**2026-10-27** — Owner decision (2026-10-27, sq-05 setup): nullTokens keys are null-vocabulary entries, case-insensitive, so the contract must say prism cannot tell NULL from null through squalify; NaN has its own vocabulary entry.

**2026-10-27** — From sq-05 review (F7): prism's D11 Constant derives as constant && (nulls == 0 || nulls == count); an all-null column has constant true. nullTokens key `null` covers NULL, Null and null (vocabulary entries); NaN has its own key. Separator rows count in nulls, not nullsExcludingAllNullRows.

**2026-10-27** — From sq-14 architect (B1): squalify follows DataBall's header grammar, prism's ColumnInfo does not: RowID( id ) -> squalify unit id (prism: ' id ', a Unit column); X( ) -> none (prism: Unit ' '); A(b(c)) -> unit 'c)' (prism: none). Names are trimmed, so D54's trailing-space near miss is invisible. Recommended: document the grammar and trimming; prism keeps its exact-name checks (D16, D54) on its own parsed header. prism mapping: Id <- nameParenUnit with unit 'id' (ordinal); Unit <- other nameParenUnit; None <- everything else.

**2026-10-27** — From sq-14 gate: digit-only paren text is still the paren convention (X(1) gives unit 1, unknownUnit); Pout(dBm)[1] is none with the whole name as base, so indexed trace columns carry no unit. State both in the consumer subset.

**2026-10-27** — From sq-05 architect: constant can be true while unique is true with distinct 3 (1, 1.0, 01: owner decision, numeric constant compares parsed values). prism's column-constant is same text with NULL as a value, so the consumer subset must spell this out.

**2026-10-27** — From sq-17 setup: table.rowClasses.allNullRows counts records whose every field is null by squalify's null vocabulary (blank, NULL, NA, N/A, NaN, ...), while prism's separator rows are all-NULL by its reader's single token. They agree on ATE export files; state the difference in the consumer subset.

**2026-10-27** — From sq-17 review (G2): ragged records count in table.rows, belong to no row class and not to field nulls, so prism's DataRows = rows - allNullRows includes ragged rows. Invariant: rows == sum(class counts) + truncated + ragged. State it in the consumer subset.

**2026-10-27** — Owner decision (2026-10-27): the contract documents; prism adapts. descriptor.md gets a Consumer subset section listing each member, its stability, and each difference from prism (case-insensitive nullTokens keys, NaN as null, constant over parsed values, allNullRows by vocabulary, trimmed names and DataBall grammar, ragged rows) with how prism derives its own view where possible. Where it cannot (exact-text constant, NULL vs null), prism keeps its own pass-1 checks (prism D3, D67). No new descriptor members.

**2026-10-27** — From sq-17 architect (H7): prism's D11 Constant must use its own data rows, i.e. constant && (nullsExcludingAllNullRows == 0 || nullsExcludingAllNullRows == count - allNullRows), not nulls and count.

items.title: squalify must have its own mark as the package icon and README image
squalify v1 must not include Parquet or its DuckDB dependency
Compact field profiles
squalify must have getting-started, user, example and developer docs
Claim degenerate delimited tables

goals:
- **Deterministic descriptor.** The same input bytes and the same squalify version give a byte-identical descriptor on every OS and CPU. No ML, LLM or network.
- **Full streaming scan with bounded memory.** Statistics are exact up to documented caps, then come from deterministic sketches that the descriptor marks as approximate.
- **v1 formats:** delimited text (preambles, annotation and units rows, repeated blocks), Touchstone, whole-file key=value/INI documents, binary (STDF V4 walk with a test catalog, plus a generic byte profile).
- **Useful for classification:** structural fingerprints (structure, layout, typed, names), layout regions, row classes, detect-rule hints, the header-unit convention, a generic `kind` label from a fixed built-in rule set, and an evidence trail for every inference.
- **Values are opt-in.** No literal data values without `--include-values`, or `--include-values-for` for named keys and columns. Header names, preamble keys, test names, and numeric and temporal statistics are always included, except for file-constant fields, whose statistics would reveal the value.
- **A stable, versioned descriptor schema** (docs/descriptor.md, frozen with a JSON Schema at v1).
- **Explained in plain language.** docs/how-it-works.md, with diagrams, plus a squalor-branded PDF render, kept current at every architectural review.
non_goals:
- Proposing DataBall configs or file types. DataBall consumes descriptors in its own roadmap.
- Classifying files against a user library of known types. The built-in `kind` label is in scope.
- ML, LLM or network use.
- Editing, repairing or converting files.
- A dependency on DataBall. The descriptor schema is the contract.
- In v1: directory or multi-file input, decompression, STDF result values, and MIR text fields.
